I farm this small piece of land here in Mangochi, and maize is what feeds my family. Last season I got a coupon from the subsidy, so I managed one bag of NPK and one bag of urea — I am hoping for the same this year, because without the coupon I cannot buy fertilizer at the full price. I keep a few goats and chickens, so I will carry their manure to the plot before the rains come, like my father taught me. I will plant the hybrid seed if the coupon brings it, otherwise I keep some grain from last harvest for seed; I weed with my wife and my older children, and only at planting time I sometimes call one or two neighbors to help me finish quickly.
